name: Git
summary: The archetype of sovereign software. Full commit history lives on your local disk, verified via cryptographic hashes, with 100% offline branching, diffing, and merging.

name: Jujutsu (jj)
summary: Next-generation version control where even conflicts and rebases are recorded as deterministic, first-class mathematical states in an undoable local operation log. Young project: the storage format is still evolving, so treat it as promising rather than canonical.

name: SQLite
summary: Library of Congress permanent archival standard. Delivers microsecond local queries with zero server daemons, zero configuration, and guaranteed backward compatibility through 2050.

name: Fossil SCM
summary: Engineered by the creator of SQLite. Packages version control, tickets, bug tracking, and wiki documentation into one durable SQLite file that runs an instant local web UI that works offline.

name: Taskwarrior
substrate: Local task database with open JSON export
summary: Command-line task manager with deterministic date and priority grammars and a complete JSON export, kept separate from long-form notes.

name: Todo.txt
substrate: Single plain-text file, one task per line
summary: The simplest possible task format: one line per task, with priority, project and context markers readable by any text tool.

name: Beancount / hledger
summary: Plain-Text Accounting (PTA). Enforces strict double-entry mathematical invariants locally without bank scraping breakages or recurring cloud subscriptions.

name: Actual Budget
summary: Local-first zero-based budgeting. Runs entirely offline against a local SQLite database and synchronizes across devices via verifiable Hybrid Logical Clock CRDT messages.

name: Obsidian
syncModel: Decoupled (Syncthing, Git, or paid first-party sync)
summary: Notes stay as standard UTF-8 Markdown files in a local folder you can edit in Vim, VS Code or bash. The app is closed-source (free for personal use), so the open files, not the application, are what earn the entry.

name: Logseq
substrate: Local Directory of Markdown / Org Files
summary: Open-source outliner that stores notes as plain Markdown or Org files in a local folder, so the same 'File Over App' guarantee holds without a proprietary application.

name: Emacs Org-Mode
summary: The grand-ancestor of sovereign personal computing. Unifies structured prose, deterministic agendas, tables, and literate programming inside immortal plain text.

name: Typst
summary: Deterministic document typesetting from plain text that recompiles multi-page documents in milliseconds, offline.

name: Hugo
summary: Static site generator that compiles a whole site from plain files in milliseconds, offline. This site is built with it.

name: Paperless-ngx
summary: Enforces the Archive Invariant: never locks or mutates original documents inside a proprietary blob. Stores untouched PDFs on disk alongside archival PDF/A files. Running it normally needs Docker plus a database and other services, which is why it sits in Tier 2.

name: LibreOffice (ODF)
summary: Full desktop office suite running 100% offline. Native files are standard zip containers holding documented XML (`content.xml`) extractable with basic POSIX unzip. The suite is large and slow to start, so it does not clearly pass the 100ms test.

name: OpenSCAD
summary: Code-first 3D solid modeling. Eliminates the non-deterministic Topological Naming Problem of GUI CAD kernels; identical script inputs yield identical meshes.

name: KiCad
summary: Electronic schematic capture and PCB design suite where every net, footprint, and trace is stored in human-readable S-expressions with zero cloud licensing.

name: NGSPICE
summary: Deterministic analog and mixed-signal circuit simulator solving differential equations directly from human-readable netlists without network dependencies.

name: REAPER
summary: Professional Digital Audio Workstation with no cloud accounts and plain-text project files parseable with standard text tools. The application itself is closed-source and paid, which keeps it out of Tier 1.

name: Darktable
summary: Non-destructive raw photography workflow. Never alters original sensor data; all exposure curves and crops reside in sibling XML sidecar files.

name: Pass
substrate: GPG-encrypted files in a plain directory
summary: Secrets live as individual GPG-encrypted files in a directory you control, with no third-party vault server.

name: KeePassXC
summary: Open-source password manager with a documented, encrypted vault file on your disk. The vault is binary, not plain text, so it ranks below Pass.

name: Syncthing
summary: The canonical decoupled synchronization layer. Replicates folders across devices with cryptographic device IDs and explicit conflict file preservation.

name: NixOS / GNU Guix
summary: While mainstream OS platforms mutate global state imperatively, NixOS/Guix treat the entire operating system as a deterministic, rollback-capable function of plain text.

name: OpenBSD
summary: Small, auditable operating system whose configuration lives in plain-text files. It is imperative rather than declarative, but every setting is inspectable and diffable.
